stops.note: Italian 'maneggiare' meant handling a horse; the riding school was the 'manège'
hand, from Latin manus, the root of maneggiare (to handle, to train horses)
adapted from Italian for the handling and training of horses
stops.meaning: the handling and training of horses

stops.note: settled as the English word for handling or being in charge of something
stops.meaning: to handle or be in charge of something

current_meaning: to be in charge of, control, or successfully handle something
